why: SC-701 makes accuracy a reviewed judgement recorded as such. A rubric written after the run would be one written to fit its answer, so the criteria are fixed here and the automated portion asserts existence, provenance resolution and rubric completion — never accuracy itself.

criteria.statement: The record's kind is one of fact, decision, convention, failure or procedure. Feature 005 introduces no sixth kind (FR-795).
The record states something. An empty claim is not knowledge.
The stored topic and value keys are already in their own canonical form, so a syntactic variant of the same subject collides with this record rather than creating a second (FR-796a).
Every cited source event exists and belongs to the session the record was derived from; zero citations are unresolvable (SC-702).
No explicit record and no supersession appears in a session that invoked no Cairn tool.

A reader given only the cited safe events would judge the claim true of this project. This is the accuracy judgement itself, and it is a human's: an automated check would be the test agreeing with itself.
The claim does not assert reasoning, intent or a cause that the event stream does not carry. Baseline 005 learns that a decision was taken and about what, never why (contracts/extraction.md §13.9).
